name: Autosomal Dominant Optic Atrophy and Congenital Deafness
aliases: Dominant Optic Neuropathy with Sensorineural Hearing Loss

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Dominant Optic Atrophy with Congenital Deafness

criteria.description: Bilateral progressive optic nerve atrophy confirmed by ophthalmological examination
Congenital or early-onset bilateral sensorineural hearing loss confirmed by audiometry
Identification of pathogenic variant in OPA1 or related gene associated with autosomal dominant optic atrophy
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Abnormal visual evoked potentials supporting optic nerve dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral optic atrophy and congenital sensorineural hearing loss with pathogenic variant in OPA1 or related gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical for confirmation; clinical features may vary in severity.

pathognomonic.notes: Progressive visual acuity loss typically begins in childhood
searchTerms: thinning of optic nerves in both eyes
damage to optic nerves causing vision loss

pathognomonic.notes: Hearing impairment present from birth or early infancy

searchTerms: blind spots in center of sight

common.symptomName: Mild to moderate progressive hearing loss
Pale optic disc on fundoscopic exam
searchTerms: optic nerve pallor on eye exam

occasional.notes: Involuntary eye movements may be present
Ringing in the ears reported in some cases

rare.symptomName: Optic disc swelling in early infancy

laboratory: Audiometric confirmation of sensorineural hearing loss
imaging: Optical coherence tomography showing retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
MRI brain usually normal or nonspecific
genetic: Occasional variants in other mitochondrial-related genes
other: Visual evoked potentials demonstrating delayed conduction
Fundoscopic examination showing optic disc pallor

distinguishingFeatures: Acute or subacute vision loss rather than gradual onset
Includes diabetes mellitus and diabetes insipidus
Optic atrophy with progressive hearing loss but accompanied by endocrine abnormalities

redFlags: Signs of systemic mitochondrial disease (e.g., diabetes, neurological decline)
references: Yu-Wai-Man P, et al. Autosomal dominant optic atrophy: clinical features and molecular genetics. Eye (Lond). 2010.
Carelli V, et al. OPA1 mutations and dominant optic atrophy: clinical and molecular aspects. J Med Genet. 2004.
Orphanet: Autosomal dominant optic atrophy and congenital deafness. ORPHA:3212.
